rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a key design choice. Config_002 tests multimodal (RNA + image) with scgpt and resnet50 encoders, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This isolates the impact of multimodal integration and advanced encoders, which are central to the problem. It balances complexity with the potential to reveal critical insights about representation and fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves 0.494 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (a simpler, linear method) affects performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation choices. It directly compares a complex (scgpt) vs. simpler (pca) encoder under identical other settings, helping determine if RNA encoding complexity is critical. This addresses uncertainty about the optimal RNA encoder while maintaining consistency in other design choices.

Existing evidence shows that using pca_n2000 (config_003) outperforms scgpt (config_002) in multimodal multiprofile settings. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation, and profile setting identical) clarifies the impact of fusion strategy. It isolates a key design choice (fusion) with minimal parameter changes, balancing exploration of critical components against exploitation of existing high-performing configurations.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models (configs 003, 006) outperform image-only models (config_001) in accuracy (0.579 vs. 0.573). Testing config_001 isolates the effect of modality by comparing a purely image-based approach to the current best multimodal setup. This clarifies whether RNA data contributes meaningfully to performance, a critical design choice. While the budget could also explore aggregation methods, testing modality is more impactful given the current performance gap.

The existing evidence shows that config_006 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.5793). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt and the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (more complex models) improves performance, isolating the impact of these components. It balances exploration by testing a promising combination of encoders while building on the success of the current best configuration.

Existing evidence shows config_006 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, transformer, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.5793). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the impact of image encoder choice. This clarifies whether upgrading the image encoder could further improve performance, addressing a key design decision with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_042) achieves high accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer and fusion from concat to weighted (config_047) further improves performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation and fusion choices, which are critical design decisions, while building on the strong foundation of the RNA/image encoder pair.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with concat fusion and transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (config_042: 0.5988). This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 RNA encoder with scvi_n200 to isolate its impact on performance. It directly compares RNA encoder choices in a high-performing setup, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of alternative encoders.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (config_048) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method to weighted isolates the effect of fusion on performance, helping determine if concat is optimal. It balances exploitation of strong RNA/image encoder choices with exploration of fusion strategies.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method to avgpool (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method the same) affects performance, isolating the impact of aggregation strategy. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation is critical for performance or if simpler methods could be equally effective.
